st.headline: Tech firms hit by AI slowdown call with Fed expected to hike rates
st.teaser: The Federal Reserve is expected to increase borrowing costs on Sept 16.
fullText: HONG KONG – Tech firms tumbled on Sept 14 after leaders of companies at the forefront of the artificial intelligence boom backed calls for a slowdown in development in the sector amid warnings that it could pose a threat to humanity.

The equity market losses were compounded by another spike in oil prices after Saudi Arabia closed a key pipeline, while US inflation data did little to lower expectations the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates this week.

Chipmakers led the selling in Asia after Anthropic chief executive officer Dario Amodei called on Sept 12 for AI companies to “pace the frontier” – or coordinate a slowdown in the technology’s development – to allow a better understanding of the risks arising.
Key among his concerns is so-called “recursive self-improvement”, or when AI can build its own next generation.
“Left unchecked, it could outrun our ability to understand and control these systems, and so must be pursued very carefully, if at all,” Amodei wrote.
His chief competitors OpenAI’s Sam Altman and xAI’s Elon Musk publicly supported him, with Musk saying “Dario is right”.
The comments came after a researcher resigned from Anthropic over fears the technology could escape human control.
Another, who did not resign, stated publicly that “we really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans”, and that he thought the chances were greater than “10 per cent within the next decade”.
While US President Donald Trump voiced opposition to the remarks and House Speaker Mike Johnson said “we don’t need everybody to panic right now”, traders sold off their tech holdings Sept 14.
Tokyo-listed tech investment titan SoftBank plunged more than 12 per cent, while chipmaker Kioxia shed more than seven per cent and Advantest more than two per cent.
South Korea’s SK hynix and Samsung were also sharply lower.
Seoul’s Kospi index led losses on broader markets, with Tokyo, Hong Kong, Shanghai, Taipei and Manila also lower.
There were gains in Sydney, Singapore and Wellington.

The selling was also being fuelled by expectations the Fed will increase borrowing costs on Sept 16 as it tries to combat stubbornly high inflation, which data showed last week remained well above the bank’s two per cent target.
The “Fed meeting sees the swaps market implying a 92 per cent probability of a hike, with 50 basis points of cumulative tightening assumed by year-end”, said Chris Weston at Pepperstone.

“Psychologically, a Fed hiking cycle rarely does risk assets many favours, particularly if both nominal and real Treasury yields are breaking to new highs and equity markets continue to find sellers into rallies.”

And National Australia Bank’s Rodrigo Catril added that the decision not to hike would “carry credibility risks and, with a hike almost fully priced, a disappointing hold could trigger a Treasury sell-off”.
The likelihood of inflation coming down any time soon has been hit by the Middle East crisis as oil prices sit well above US$100 a barrel.

Both main contracts jumped more than two per cent on Sept 14 after Riyadh shut its East-West pipeline following drone attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels, while a merchant vessel was struck in the Strait of Hormuz.
The Houthis have been cementing their hold on the Bab Al-Mandab strait, a vital shipping corridor linking Europe and Asia that has been used as an alternative to Hormuz.
The conflict sent average diesel prices in the United States above US$6 a gallon on Sept 11 for the first time, a shock increase for a key fuel in the transport and agriculture sectors.
Meanwhile, Oman said it had postponed talks between Iran and Gulf states on the future of the strategic waterway, a vital route for a large share of the world’s seaborne oil trade. AFP

cna.headline: Fans of The Early Spring think Jing Boran's character is based on Chinese singer Liu Lian
cna.teaser: Here are all the similarities they found to keep that theory going.
fullText: Chinese drama The Early Spring is topping Netflix charts in Singapore. The workplace romance drama follows sharp-tongued advertising executive Luan Nian (Jing Boran) and his secret office romance with newcomer Shang Zhitao (Sun Qian).
But as viewers get increasingly invested in the couple, Chinese netizens have started obsessing over how reel life may have found inspiration from real life.
Specifically, is the main character Luan Nian based on award-winning Chinese singer Liu Lian? And they've got facts to back up their theory.
Long before many people knew Liu Lian as a singer, she was working in advertising.
The Peking University graduate joined Ogilvy Beijing as an intern in 2012 after giving up the opportunity to pursue postgraduate studies through direct admission.
Her starting salary? 3,500 yuan (US$521) a month.
Liu Lian eventually worked her way up to creative director and remained with the advertising giant until 2022.
Luan Nian is also a senior creative at a major advertising agency, the fictitious Lime Advertising.
And like Liu Lian, he has ties to Peking University.
Then comes the detail that really sent netizens down the rabbit hole.
In The Early Spring, Taotao happens to be Shang Zhitao's nickname.
To add to that, Shang Zhitao also owns a Samoyed in the drama, though hers is called Luke.
The comparisons eventually reached Liu Lian herself. While chatting with actress Wang Gege on a podcast, she addressed the theory with amusement.
"I really want to ask the original author. Am I actually the inspiration?" she joked.
And The Early Spring has apparently done more than make Liu Lian wonder whether parts of her life somehow ended up in a drama.
It's also resurrected an old group chat. According to Liu Lian, the chat with her former Ogilvy colleagues had been practically dead for years.
Then The Early Spring became a hit and everyone suddenly started digging out and sharing old photos from their advertising days.
While working at Ogilvy, Liu Lian formed a vocal jazz duo called Mr Miss with fellow Peking University alumnus Du Kai.
Their debut album won Best Vocal Group at the 28th Golden Melody Awards, in a category that also included Power Station and Grasshopper.
Liu was later named to Forbes China's 30 Under 30 list in 2018 and gained wider recognition after appearing on the third season of Sisters Who Make Waves in 2022.
So, is she the real-life Luan Nian? For now, there's no confirmation that Liu Lian inspired the character.

listening.title: Singapore's Push for AI in Schools
listening.transcript: As Singapore continues its push toward a smart nation, local classrooms are undergoing a digital transformation. Artificial intelligence tools are being trialled in primary schools to provide personalized learning feedback for students. Educators argue that this technology does not replace teachers, but rather acts as a co-pilot to help identify learning gaps early. Parents, however, remain cautiously optimistic about the screen-time increase.

economistArticle.title: Wanted: new business, finance and economics interns
paras: The landscape of business and financial journalism has never been more demanding, nor has it ever been more critical. As global markets react to shifting geopolitical alignments and rapid technological disruptions, the need for sharp, analytical reporting is paramount. The Economist, in its ongoing search for fresh analytical minds, is once again inviting applications for the Marjorie Deane internship, a coveted launchpad for aspiring financial journalists.

Named after a legendary editor who spent decades shaping the publication's rigorous standards, the Marjorie Deane Foundation aims to promote high-caliber financial journalism. Successful applicants are not merely expected to fetch coffee or summarize press releases; they are thrown into the deep end, tasked with deciphering complex market trends, examining corporate balance sheets, and translating dense economic jargon into crystal-clear prose.

In an era dominated by superficial clickbait and instant social-media hot takes, the value of patient, evidence-based reporting cannot be overstated. Today’s aspiring interns must possess more than just a passing interest in interest rates or corporate mergers. They must display an insatiable curiosity about how the world works, paired with the intellectual humility to admit what they do not yet know and the tenacity to find out.

Crucially, the internship offers a rare glimpse into the collaborative alchemy of the newsroom. Interns work alongside seasoned editors, receiving unvarnished feedback that shapes their writing and refines their critical thinking. For those who survive and thrive under this constructive crucible, the experience often paves the way to a permanent career at some of the world's most influential publications.

The application process itself is a test of mettle, requiring a short essay that demonstrates both analytical rigour and a distinct prose style. For those ready to dissect the complexities of modern capitalism, this internship is not just a line on a resume, but an initiation into a craft that remains vital to a well-functioning democracy.
economistArticle.cn:
商业和财经新闻的格局从未像现在这样要求苛刻，也从未像现在这样至关重要。随着全球市场对不断变化的的地缘政治格局和快速的技术颠覆做出反应，对敏锐、分析性报道的需求至关重要。《 could 》杂志在不断寻找新鲜的分析型人才，再次邀请申请马乔里·迪恩（Marjorie Deane）实习项目，这是有志于成为财经记者的令人向往的跳板。

该基金会以一位花了数十年时间塑造该刊物严谨标准的传奇编辑命名，旨在推广高水平的财经新闻。成功的申请者不仅仅是被期望去端咖啡或总结新闻稿；他们会被推入深水区，任务是破译复杂的市场趋势，审查公司资产负债表，并将晦涩的经济术语翻译成水晶般清晰的散文。

在这个被肤浅的标题党和即时社交媒体热议所主导的时代，耐心、基于证据的报道的价值怎么强调都不为过。今天有抱负的实习生必须拥有的不仅仅是对利率或企业并购的短暂兴趣。他们必须对世界的运作方式表现出一种无法满足的好奇心，同时具备承认自己还不知道的事情的求知谦逊，以及找出答案的韧性。

至关重要的是，该实习提供了一个罕见的机会，得以一窥编辑室合作的神奇融合。实习生与经验丰富的编辑并肩工作，接受不加粉饰的反馈，这些反馈塑造了他们的写作并磨炼了他们的批判性思维。对于那些在这种建设性的严峻考验中生存并茁壮成长的人来说，这段经历往往为在世界上一些最具影响力的出版物获得永久职业生涯铺平道路。

申请过程本身就是对勇气的考验，需要写一篇短文，展示分析的严谨性和独特的散文风格。对于那些准备剖析现代资本主义复杂性的人来说，这次实习不仅是简历上的一行字，更是进入一门对运转良好的民主制度仍然至关重要的手艺的开始。

gems.s: In an era dominated by superficial clickbait and instant social-media hot takes, the value of patient, evidence-based reporting cannot be overstated.
gems.why: This sentence uses sharp contrast ('superficial clickbait' vs 'patient, evidence-based reporting') to emphasize the growing necessity of quality journalism in modern times. 这句话通过强烈的对比（‘肤浅的标题党’与‘耐心、基于证据的报道’），突显了现代社会中高质量新闻日益增长的必要性。
